messages:
Olivia (People Ops): Heads-up — we need to finalize reviewer calendar blocks and timezone coverage for the upcoming performance review window. Proposed review window: May 6–17. Please read and respond with any hard blockers by EOD Thursday. Link to signup sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REVIEW-SIGNUP

Ravi (People Ops): Quick summary of what we need from each manager/reviewer: 1) Block 2h/day reviewer time on calendar for at least 8 business days during the window. 2) Pick at least two calibration slots. 3) Update the "reviewer-availability" tab with timezone + preferred shift window.

Jordan (Eng Mgr): For APAC folks — can we confirm a rotation so no one does all the late-night slots? I can take one late slot per week but not more than that.

Olivia (People Ops): Yep — plan is a 3-shift rotation: Americas (PT/MT), EMEA (UTC+0–+3), APAC (IST+ to JST). We’ll try to assign at most 2 late slots per person across the window.

Tasha (SWE): I can cover two APAC late shifts (8pm–10pm my local) but I need to keep a 1h deep-work block in mornings. Also can we avoid scheduling calibration immediately after sprint demos?

Ravi (People Ops): Noted — we'll avoid 11:00–13:00 local demo windows when possible. Also: form write access will be open until May 5 23:59 UTC. After that reviewers can only comment, not edit the review forms.

Evan (Recruiter): Small ask — can we surface any reviewers who are on hiring interviews during the window so hiring ops can avoid double-booking? I’ll sync with people calendar exports.

Olivia (People Ops): Good call. Please add those blocks to the sheet under "conflicts" and set calendar events to "busy". We'll run a conflict check script on Friday and notify managers of overlaps.

reviewer-ops-bot: Reminder set: "Conflict check script run" scheduled for Friday 09:00 UTC.

Jordan (Eng Mgr): What’s the fallback if a reviewer cancels <24h before their slot? We had last-minute dropouts last cycle and it was messy.

Ravi (People Ops): We'll spin up an "overflow reviewer pool" with 6 people who agreed to be on-call. If someone cancels inside 24h, we auto-assign from the pool and send calendar invites. We’ll prioritize people in the same timezone band.

Olivia (People Ops): Action item — managers, please confirm your on-call overflow nominee(s) in the sheet by Wed noon. Also update headcounts: how many reviews/day each person is expected to complete (target 3–5 depending on role).

Tasha (SWE): Can we get a sample calendar invite for reviewers so the invite text is consistent?

Olivia (People Ops): Yes — use this template when creating events (paste into calendar description):

```
Subject: PR Reviewer Session — [Your Name]
When: [Date] [Start]–[End] (block 2 hours)
Location: Google Meet link
Description: Blocked for review reading and calibration. Please read assigned review packets before the slot. Bring notes and be ready for 20m calibration discussion at the top of the slot.
Notes: If you must cancel <24h, mark the sheet and tag @people-ops for auto-assign from overflow pool.
```

Ravi (People Ops): We’ll also add a short checklist to the invite: 1) Open review forms, 2) Run evaluation rubric on sample, 3) Join calibration call link pinned in the sheet.

Olivia (People Ops): Final deadlines reminder: signups + conflicts due Thu EOD; overflow nominees due Wed noon; final calendar publish Fri 12:00 UTC. If anyone expects PTO during May 6–17, please mark it today.

Jordan (Eng Mgr): :thumbsup: sounds good. I'll nominate two folks from my team.

Tasha (SWE): Done — added my availability and conflicts.

Evan (Recruiter): Will export interview slots and drop them in the sheet by tomorrow morning.

Olivia (People Ops): Thanks all — I'll run the conflict check and post an updated calendar after the Friday job. If anything urgent, ping @people-ops or DM me directly. :party_parrot:
